issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns about missing unzip but does not exit
issues.detail: The script checks `if ! command -v unzip`, echoes a message, and then continues running. When it later hits `unzip -q ...`, the script will die with a cryptic error. Either exit non-zero on the missing-dependency check or drop it. Same for the usage block: it prints usage on bad argc and then falls through to `realpath $1` with no args. A small filter-style script should fail fast on bad input.

issues.description: Unquoted command substitutions in realpath calls
issues.detail: `extract_dir=$(realpath $1)` and `zip_dir=$(realpath ${2:-$extract_dir})` are unquoted. Any path with a space silently breaks. The script otherwise runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so the inconsistency is a real foot-gun for users on Mac or Windows-mounted shares. Quote them: `"$1"` and `"${2:-$extract_dir}"`.

issues.description: Three near-identical extraction blocks beg to be a loop
issues.detail: The TAL_ASR-1/2/3 stanzas are copy-paste with one varying triple: (archive_name, sentinel_dir, human_name). This is the canonical 'data dominates' case: put the three rows in a tiny here-doc table and loop over them, the way `local/data.sh` already does for its prepare_kaldi calls. Three nearly identical blocks invite drift the next time someone adjusts one.

issues.description: Transcript sanitization is a chain of `sed`s where one would do
issues.detail: `sed 's/Ａ/A/g' | sed 's/#//g' | sed 's/=//g' | sed 's/、//g' | sed 's/，//g' | sed 's/？//g' | sed 's/。//g' | sed 's/[ ][ ]*$//g'` spawns seven processes per line where a single `sed -e ... -e ...` (or one `tr -d`) covers it. Small thing, but it is exactly the kind of filter-shape cleanup the Unix tradition would flag.

issues.description: wav.flist is parsed three times instead of once
issues.detail: `data.sh` runs the same `sed -e 's/\.wav//' wav.flist | awk -F '/' ...` pipeline three times to produce utt.list, utt_uttid, and utt2spk. One `awk` pass over wav.flist can emit all three files via `print ... > file` redirections. Same data, one transform. This is the textbook 'choose the data structure and the algorithm is obvious' move.

README links to `./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml` but the file lives at `./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml` (no `train/` subdir). A small documentation defect, but it will mislead the next reader.

issues.description: Inline subject-label scrubs are dataset-specific magic strings
issues.detail: The seven Chinese-punctuation/full-width-A substitutions are dataset-specific normalization buried in the middle of the data prep. Moving them into a tiny `local/normalize_text.sh` (or one `python -c` call) makes the transform reusable and lets the data.sh stay a pipeline of clearly named steps. Not load-bearing, but it is the difference between a script and a filter.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE overall. This is a standard ESPnet egs2 recipe, mostly symlinks and YAML, and the YAMLs are appropriately boring. The two real shell scripts are where the only cleanup lies. `download_and_untar.sh` has a broken dependency check (warns, then proceeds to crash), unquoted realpath args, and three copy-pasted extraction blocks that want to be a loop over a tiny table. `local/data.sh` re-parses the same wav.flist three times when one awk pass would do, and chains seven seds where one would do; the transcript-normalization step also wants to be a named filter rather than inline magic. None of this blocks the recipe; the model trains and the CER numbers are reasonable. Fix the unzip-check fall-through (P1), quote the realpaths (P1), and the rest is housekeeping.
